_comment: What each TTL pin is used for, and what a TTL module syncs with. A pin's use follows from its mode (uses / roles below); a sync line can name the system it feeds (ttl.pins.<gpio>.system, sync_systems), and the module's application (ephys_sync / neurologger_sync / mixed) is worked out from that: rig check, session record and the External sync choice use it. One source for the module, the controller and the frontend. plans/ttl-applications-ephys-sync.md. external_sync: what a session can be synchronised with (New Session 'External sync').

mixed.label: General TTL
mixed.description: No sync line with a system set.

ephys_sync.label: Ephys sync
ephys_sync.description: Its sync line feeds an ephys acquisition system (Open Ephys).

neurologger_sync.label: Neurologger sync
neurologger_sync.description: Its sync line feeds a wireless neurologger.

sync.label: Sync line
sync.description: Pseudorandom pulses that another system records alongside its own data, so it can be aligned with every camera and microphone. Optionally say which system.

experiment_marker.label: Experiment marker
experiment_marker.description: Goes active when the recording starts and inactive when it stops.

protocol.label: Protocol output
protocol.description: Driven by the session protocol. Shown in the Protocol designer under its label.

experiment_start.label: Start pulse
experiment_start.description: One pulse when the recording starts.

marker_in.label: Event input
marker_in.description: Logs each edge on an input line, e.g. a lever press or another system's trigger.

regular_pulses.label: Regular pulses
regular_pulses.description: A pulse every so often while recording.

clock.label: Clock
clock.description: A square wave for the whole recording.

manual.label: Manual output
manual.description: Held inactive; only Test and the REST pulse endpoint drive it.

ephys.label: Ephys (Open Ephys)
ephys.description: An Open Ephys acquisition system records alongside SAVIOUR; an Ephys sync TTL module sends it the sync pulses.

neurologger.label: Neurologger
neurologger.description: A wireless neurologger records alongside SAVIOUR; a Neurologger sync TTL module sends it the sync pulses.
